series.title: Myth vs fact
series.about: Strike-through myths next to the real answer. Study habits, exam technique and subject misconceptions. Built for saves and 'wait, really?' shares. Every fact is checked against the syllabus or mark-scheme conventions.
series.check: Facts must stay accurate: re-check against the syllabus before editing.

posts.caption:
Study myths we need to stop believing. 🙅

Number 3 is the big one: past papers aren't the end of revision, they ARE revision. Start them as soon as you finish a chapter.

slides.title: study myths, busted
items: You need 10 hours a day to get an A*
A few focused hours of questions beat a whole day of re-reading.
Highlighting = studying
Testing yourself is what makes it stick.
Past papers are for the last month
Start topical questions the week you finish a chapter.
An all-nighter before helps
Sleep is when your brain stores what you learned.

posts.caption:
Exam technique myths, busted. ✍️

There's no negative marking in these papers, so a blank answer is a guaranteed zero. Always write something sensible.

slides.title: exam myths, busted
items: Examiners like long answers
They mark points. One clear point per mark is enough.
If the answer's right, working doesn't matter
'Show your working' questions can lose marks without it, and wrong answers still earn method marks.
If you don't know it, leave it blank
No negative marking. Write something sensible.
Rounding as you go is fine
Keep full values and round only at the end.

posts.caption:
Physics myths that cost marks. ⚡

'Current gets used up' is the one examiners see most. Current is the same all the way round a series circuit; it's energy that gets transferred.

slides.title: physics myths, busted
items: Heavier things fall faster
With no air resistance, everything falls with the same acceleration.
Current gets used up in a circuit
Current is the same all round a series circuit. Energy is transferred.
Mass and weight are the same thing
Mass is in kg. Weight is a force in N: W = mg.
Heat rises
Hot fluids rise (convection). Thermal energy moves in every direction.

posts.caption:
Maths myths that cost marks. 🧮

Save this and check your last paper for number 2. It's everywhere.

slides.title: maths myths, busted
items: x² = 9 means x = 3
x = 3 or x = −3.
(a + b)² = a² + b²
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
Probability 0.5 means it happens every other time
It means half the time in the long run.
Multiplying always makes a number bigger
× 0.5 halves it. Multiplying by a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller.

posts.caption:
Computer Science myths, busted. 💻

The kilobyte one appears on real papers: KiB = 1024 bytes, kB = 1000 bytes. Read which one the question uses.

slides.title: CS myths, busted
items: A kilobyte is always 1024 bytes
1 KiB = 1024 bytes. 1 kB = 1000 bytes. Check the question.
RAM keeps your work when the power goes off
RAM is volatile. Storage (like an SSD) keeps it.
Validation checks the data is correct
It checks the data is sensible. Verification checks it was entered or copied correctly.
Lossy compression is always bad
It makes files much smaller, and you often can't notice what's lost.
